tasks.short: Monitor actual sound and image quality

steps.what: Check the actual show, auditorium and intended projection/sound format on the existing cinema control display before monitoring quality.
inputs: Actual show and auditorium configuration

steps.what: Observe the actual projected image in the auditorium, checking focus, framing, brightness, colour and visible image faults throughout the required actual checks.
inputs: Actual monitoring context from s1
Actual projected image and auditorium conditions

steps.what: Listen to the actual reproduced sound in the auditorium and assess level, clarity, synchronisation and channel behaviour against the actual sound standard.
inputs: Actual show context from s1
Actual auditorium sound

steps.what: Determine whether the actual sound and image projection quality meet the required standards, investigating ambiguous faults with further direct checks rather than accepting a normal server status alone.
inputs: Actual image and sound findings from s2-s3
Actual required standards
outputs: Actual quality assessment and identified unresolved defects

tasks.design: Retain the actual visual and auditory monitoring. OTHER means actual projector, sound equipment and auditorium. Native server status and meter displays were considered but do not establish that the audience receives acceptable image and sound. No new observation record is added here. The explicit report-writing task 8048 in this same answer contains its own actual capture step for real inspection findings; no saving is transferred to that task for these retained observations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Normal playback status does not prove actual focus, auditorium sound or synchronisation quality.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing status displays support context but no changed actual quality-check action is established.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults and auditorium effects can be missed by status telemetry.
tasks.human_edge: See and hear the actual audience-facing result and identify ambiguity.

ambition.what: Perform the actual existing quality monitoring.

tasks.altitude: Understand the difference between equipment status and delivered quality.

evidence.claim: Playback status alone does not replace direct checks of actual projected image and auditorium sound.

assumptions: This task allocates active quality-check labour, not unattended film runtime.
No separate manual report or send is established within these direct checks; actual report capture is explicit in task 8048, and no observation saving is claimed in either task.
No unprovided camera or microphone analysis system is treated as existing input.
unknowns: Actual quality-check procedure and existing instrument coverage
research_questions: Observe actual checks and distinguish direct delivered-quality assessment from server-status reading.

already_counted.description: Actual show-context check, image observation, listening and final quality assessment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: After separating context lookup, actual image checks, listening and quality assessment, native telemetry removes none of the established checks. No new written record or automatic defect report is invented; actual report capture is separately retained in the explicit report task. All monitoring labour remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the actual current opening schedule and facility rules in {CALENDAR}; a native current-day view removes finding the correct dated schedule while interpretation and any changed instructions remain.
inputs: Actual current facility schedule and opening rules
outputs: Actual opening time and required opening conditions

steps.what: Make the actual required opening checks of the cinema facilities, access routes, equipment readiness and current exceptions before admitting use.
inputs: Actual opening conditions from s1
Actual facilities and any current exception
outputs: Actual opening readiness or unresolved hold

steps.what: Physically open the actual facilities according to the current rules and schedule, carrying out the required local access and setup actions after the actual opening checks.
inputs: Actual opening readiness and instructions from s1-s2
outputs: Actual facilities opened or kept closed for an unresolved condition

steps.what: At the actual closing phase, look up the current last-show finish and any late schedule change in {CALENDAR}; a native auditorium/day filter supplies the relevant finish entry while checking the actual change remains.
inputs: Actual current end-of-day show schedule and changes
outputs: Actual closing time and current exception information

steps.what: Check the actual cinema facilities at closing for remaining people, ongoing activity, equipment and access conditions before completing the actual closing sequence.
inputs: Actual closing time and exceptions from s4
Actual facilities and people still present
outputs: Actual closing readiness or continued attendance required

steps.what: Physically close and secure the actual facilities under the rules after actual occupants and activities are resolved, performing the required local shutdown and locking actions.
inputs: Actual closing readiness from s5
Actual closing rules
outputs: Actual facilities closed and secured or unresolved condition retained

tasks.design: Use native current-day and last-show views for actual repeated schedule lookup. The opening lookup retains more interpretation of rules; the closing filter removes a larger fraction of locating the relevant final entry. Keep all physical readiness, opening, occupant checks and closing work. No automatic door/alarm command, newly mandated checklist write or post-closing record is introduced. Closing lookup occurs at closing, not once before the day's activities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staff may locate the correct day and final show within a larger existing schedule.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calendar filters can show the actual current day and auditorium's final entry.
tasks.still_hard: A scheduled finish does not prove people have left or a facility is ready to close.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve actual occupants and exceptions before physically securing the building.

ambition.what: Open and close the actual existing facility.

tasks.altitude: Distinguish planned times from actual readiness.

evidence.claim: Native schedule filters can reduce locating dated entries without performing physical readiness checks or facility opening/closing.

assumptions: Conditional baseline includes actual repeated schedule lookup; shares are estimated active-work proportions, not elapsed opening hours.
Opening lookup removes only 1 hour of locating the day; rule reading remains. Closing lookup removes 2 hours of finding the final relevant entry; actual late-change checks remain.
A facility already displaying the relevant entries gets no new saving.
No separate written opening/closing record is established; none is invented.
unknowns: Actual schedule display and time spent locating entries
research_questions: Observe opening and closing separately and determine whether dated-entry lookup is genuinely manual.

already_counted.description: Retained schedule interpretation and actual readiness, opening, closing checks and physical securing

incremental.description: Maintain the auditorium/day view and test schedule-change display

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conservative case already displays today's times and final show or has no repeated lookup; no change is claimed. Where manual dated-entry location exists, the opening view removes 1 hour and closing filter removes 2, less 0.5 hour upkeep. Their cuts differ because the opening step includes rule interpretation while the closing lookup mainly finds the final entry. Physical work remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare inspection reports, attendance sheets and logs

steps.what: Select the actual shows, auditoriums, reporting period and required film inspection, attendance and logbook formats in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
inputs: Actual shows and required existing record formats
outputs: Actual selected show identifiers and reporting scope

steps.what: Import the actual existing ticketing attendance totals by the selected show identifiers into the attendance sheet using the supported native export/import between ticketing and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
inputs: Actual selected show identifiers from s1
Actual existing ticketing attendance records
outputs: Draft attendance rows with source show identifiers and totals

steps.what: Import the actual existing digital cinema server show-start, show-end and playback event fields into the working logbook in {OPS_SYSTEM} by the selected show identifiers.
inputs: Actual selected show identifiers from s1
Actual existing cinema server event records
outputs: Draft actual show-event log rows or explicit absent-source flags

steps.what: Write the actual film inspection findings, image/sound defects, operator remarks and any manually observed show events into {OPS_SYSTEM}, capturing what the projectionist actually observed rather than inferring it from playback status.
inputs: Actual film inspection and projection-quality observations
Draft attendance and show-event rows from s2-s3
outputs: Actual supplied inspection findings and operator log remarks

steps.what: Format the actual attendance rows, supplied inspection findings and show-event rows into the required film inspection report, attendance sheet and logbook layouts using native {OPS_SYSTEM} record views and print templates.
inputs: Actual selected record formats from s1
Actual imported/supplied rows and remarks from s2-s4
outputs: Complete draft film inspection report, attendance sheet and logbook

steps.what: Check and correct the actual complete reports, attendance sheets and logbooks for show/date matching, attendance meaning, missing events and faithful inspection findings, manually resolving import or source gaps.
inputs: Complete draft records from s5
Actual source attendance/events and actual inspection findings
outputs: Actual reconciled and corrected projection records

steps.what: Save the actual completed inspection reports, attendance sheets and logbook entries in the same {OPS_SYSTEM} record area.
inputs: Actual corrected records from s6

tasks.design: Use separate native attendance import, show-event import and final record formatting. OTHER means the existing ticketing system and digital cinema server. Their normal sales/entry transactions and server event generation are the existing source producers and remain unchanged. The projectionist's actual inspection findings are explicitly captured in s4 and never replaced with server telemetry. The final record correction step retains source-gap and failed-import repair. Same-system save stays small, manual and ungated; no report send is introduced where none is required.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual attendance and show-event fields can be copied into several report and log formats by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported exact show-identifier imports and native record templates can reuse those existing fields.
tasks.still_hard: Ticket sales are not always actual attendance, film defects require actual inspection and a digital show log does not describe a physical film print.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile what actually happened and record genuine inspection findings.

ambition.what: Prepare the existing actual projection records.

tasks.altitude: Specify exact show identities, attendance definitions and source limitations.

evidence.claim: Exact ticketing/show-log imports and native report templates can reuse existing fields while actual film inspection remarks and source reconciliation remain human work.

assumptions: Conditional compatible cinema baseline actually copies attendance and digital show-event fields and manually formats records; shares are unmeasured estimates.

Ticketing records are produced by normal existing sales/entry work; digital event records by existing server operation. No extra seller capture or new sensor programme is assumed, and no producer labour saving is claimed.
Task 8030's actual image/sound observation remains fully retained. Actual film inspection also continues unchanged; this task counts the actual record capture in s4.
All failed-import and missing-source manual repair remains in s4/s6. A film-only venue without server events cannot receive the s3 reduction.
No general staff approval or independent sign-off is added for saving the author's own records.
unknowns: Actual attendance definition, show-identifier compatibility and digital versus film mix
research_questions: Trace a real show into all three records and verify attendance meaning, source timestamps and actual manual copying.
Replay a missing-event/import-failure case and time the actual retained correction.

already_counted.description: Actual scope selection, new inspection/event remark capture, full reconciliation and repair, and ordinary record save

incremental.description: Maintain exact show-id mappings, attendance definition and required record layouts

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conservative case retains the full 20-hour attendance transcription and 15-hour show-event entry because paper attendance and physical film have no compatible feeds; the existing electronic output layout can still remove 15 hours formatting, less 2 upkeep. In the compatible actual digital/ticketing case, exact imports and formatting remove 50 hours, less 2. Actual inspection, new remarks and complete source-gap repair remain retained in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Know how actual projection quality differs from equipment status, and maintain precise show identities in existing records.
role.ambitious_version: A projectionist who spends less time copying actual show fields while keeping direct quality checks, real facility work and truthful inspection records.
